human_decisions.answer: No. Cross-team ticket assignment to a Support Agent is not permitted in the first release. A Support Agent may be assigned tickets only within their single primary support team. No cross-team assignment exception, temporary access mechanism, separate approval authority, or additional permission/grant mechanism will be introduced. Tenant Admin may route tickets across teams within their own tenant, but must assign an Agent only if that Agent belongs to the ticket's assigned team. Tenant Admin manages Agent team membership and may change an Agent's primary team through the authorized team-membership workflow. Any resulting assignment changes must be validated and audited. Access must be immediately revoked when an Agent is reassigned, loses primary-team membership, or otherwise loses the required tenant, team, or ticket authorization. All assignment and reassignment operations must enforce server-side tenant and team membership validation. Unauthorized assignments must be denied and audited.

The New → Open transition is permitted for the following roles, subject to server-side authorization and ticket scope validation:
1. Support Agent: May transition a New ticket to Open only when the ticket is currently assigned to that Agent and the Agent retains valid primary-team and tenant authorization.
2. Support Manager: May transition a New ticket to Open only when the ticket belongs to one of the Manager's currently assigned teams, including team-assigned tickets without an individual Agent.
3. Tenant Admin: May transition a New ticket to Open for any ticket within their own tenant, including completely unassigned tickets, as part of their existing tenant-wide ticket management and central-triage authority.
Platform Admin is not permitted to perform routine tenant ticket-business status transitions. Ticket creation alone does not grant a separate permission to transition New to Open. A ticket creator must independently satisfy the applicable role, assignment, tenant, and team authorization requirements. The backend must revalidate the user's current authorization, ticket tenant, team, assignment, and current status for every transition. Reject unauthorized requests and all undefined transitions by default. Record successful transitions in ticket activity history and audit logs.
